docs.title: SolarNode Filter Simulator
docs.text:
This handbook provides guides and reference documentation for the SolarNetwork SolarNode Filter Simulator. This is a browser-based tool to help create, edit, view, and debug the SolarNode Datum Filter processing runtime.

Datum Filters are services in SolarNode that can filter, augment, and modify datum in real-time, as they are created. Datum Filters can also create new datum and interact with controls. They are very flexible and powerful, but as you add more than just a few filters it can be cumbersome to keep track of what all of them are doing and reason about their effects on the datum processing pipeline.

This tool helps you develop and maintain complex filter configurations using an intuitive, interactive flow-chart style diagram. You can drag and drop filters onto the diagram, inspect and modify their settings, and then simulate sending datum through them. You can even import the settings configuration from a real SolarNode, make changes, test the changes, export the settings back out when you are happy, and finally import the updated settings back into your SolarNode.

docs.title: Creating a simulation
docs.text: To create a simulation you can create one from scratch just using the Simulator, and you can also import settings from a SolarNode to start with its filter settings.

docs.title: Create from scratch
docs.text:
To create a simulation from scratch, drag your desired filters from the Filter palette onto the Canvas.

A new, empty simulation.

Drop filters onto a connection line to insert the filter into that position within the overall flow. Drop filters anywhere else on the canvas if you would like to configure its settings without it participating in the main flow.

docs.title: Import filter settings from SolarNode
docs.text:
You can import the settings from a SolarNode that already has filters configured, so you can then simulate that exact setup. From SolarNode, go to Settings > Backups > Settings Backup & Restore and click the Export to file button to download the node's settings as a CSV file.

The exported file will include all of SolarNode's settings. The SolarNode Filter Simulator will ignore non-filter settings so you do not have to worry about any other settings are included in the export.

Now in the Simulator, click on the Import settings button in the Control pane and select the file you exported from SolarNode.

docs.title: Making changes
docs.text:
Click on individual filters on the canvas to inspect its settings in the Inspector. You can modify the filter's settings there.

You can remove a filter from the canvas by selecting it, then typing the Backspace or Del key.

You can use Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z to undo your changes as you go.

docs.title: Getting your bearings
docs.text:
When you first visit the application, you are presented with four main panes:

  • Setup (top left) - where you configure the overall parameters of the simulation, such as the datum to run through the filters, node metadata, and placeholders.
  • Control (middle left) - where you can start the simulation as well as import or export the filter settings as CSV files.
  • Filter Palette (bottom left) - a list of the available filters that you can drag onto the canvas.
  • Canvas (middle) - a flow chart style visualization of the simulation.
  • Inspector - shows the editable properties of a filter after you click on one in the canvas.

docs.title: Setup pane
docs.text:
The various tab views within the Setup pane.

The Setup pane is where you configure the overall SolarNode simulation universe. At a minimum you must provide the initial datum to send into the filter execution flow. These initial datum represent data captured from SolarNode Datum Sources that read from devices like meters and power inverters.

The History, Environment, Node Metadata, User Metadata, and Datum Metadata tabs in this pane allow you to configure other simulated SolarNode services like Metadata, Placeholders, Operational Modes, Local State, and more. Generally you need to configure everything your filters expect to be available when they run in SolarNode.

docs.title: Control pane
docs.text:
The Control pane is where you can:

  • import filter settings from a SolarNode
  • export the simulation's filter settings, so you can apply them to a SolarNOde
  • add external filter settings, like those contributed by solarnode-config-* packages in SolarNodeOS; these are not exported with your simulation settings
  • run (or debug) the simulation

The Entry Point is the name of the filter to pass the input datum to when you run the simulation. Typically this is the Main Filter Chain, but you can actually specify any filter in the simulation.

docs.title: Filter palette
docs.text: The Filter palette shows you all the available filters you can use in the simulator. Simply drag a filter from the palette over to the canvas to add it to the simulation. Drop the filter on any connector line between filters to insert that filter into the execution flow at that point.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: The SolarNode Filter Simulator is an application you run on your own workstation. When you run it, it will open up in your preferred browser. If you close your browser window and want to go back to the application, it also prints out the URL to visit so you can click on that, or copy/paste it into your preferred browser.

docs.title: Homebrew (macOS/Linux)
docs.text:
You can install the sn-filter-sim native binary using Homebrew by adding the SolarNetwork/tap tap's solarnode-filter-sim package:

# add the SolarNetwork tap
brew tap solarnetwork/tap

# trust the SolarNetwork tap
brew trust solarnetwork/tap

# install the solarnode-filter-sim package
brew install solarnode-filter-sim

After that, the solarnode-filter-sim tool should be available:

solarnode-filter-sim

SolarNode Filter Simulator (0.7.0) started, visit
http://localhost:2008

docs.title: Manual (macOS/Linux/Windows)
docs.text:
Download the latest release from Github. Download the appropriate binary archive for your system, if available. Otherwise download the JAR file.

Linux (arm64)Linux (x64)macOS (Apple Silicon)Windows (x64)

Download the tar archive named like solarnode-filter-sim-X.Y.Z-linux-arm64.tar.gz. Use tar to expand the archive, and then move the extracted sn-filter-sim application somewhere on your PATH like /usr/local/bin.

Download the tar archive named like solarnode-filter-sim-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.tar.gz. Use tar to expand the archive, and then move the extracted sn-filter-sim application somewhere on your PATH like /usr/local/bin.

Download the tar archive named like solarnode-filter-sim-X.Y.Z-darwin-arm64.tar.gz. Double-click to expand the archive, or use tar, and then move the extracted sn-filter-sim application somewhere on your PATH like /usr/local/bin.

Download the tar archive named like solarnode-filter-sim-X.Y.Z-windows-amd64.tar.gz. Expand the archive, and then move the extracted sn-filter-sim.exe application somewhere on your PATH.

If a binary is not available for your system, you can download the Java JAR, which requires you to have Java 25+ installed.

Java JAR

Download the JAR file named like sn-filter-sim-X.Y.Z.jar. You can execute this using java -jar sn-filter-sim-X.Y.Z.jar.

docs.title: Running a simulation
docs.text:
Once you have a simualtion set up, run it by clicking the Run button in the Control pane:

Execute a simulation by clicking the Run button.

docs.title: Simulation result
docs.text:
After running a simulation, an Execution Flow pane will appear below the Canvas, with the results of the simulation.

An example simulation. In this run 5 datum were passed through the filters, and a Downsample filter discarded the first 4, emitting a modified "downsampled" 5th datum.
